lessons.title: Your Claude workspace with Projects, Memory and Artifacts
lessons.subtitle: From a chat window to a maintained workspace

props.title: Build your first Claude Project brief
props.scenario: Write a system prompt with the approved context this Project reuses. Case-specific and confidential data stay out.

role.hint: Who is Claude in this Project? For example, sales assistant, HR business partner or workshop manager.

context.hint: Company, industry, size, products and communication rules, only what may be stored persistently.

task.hint: Which three to five tasks does Claude support here, such as quotations, follow-up questions or analysis?

format.hint: Standard format, such as Markdown, bullet points or a word limit per answer.

constraints.hint: What is off-limits? Customer data, unapproved prices, promotional claims, tool recommendations.

sections.title: Why a single chat is not enough
sections.content:
Every new chat knows only what is in it. Retyping role, organization and style costs time and makes results inconsistent.

A Project holds a maintained system prompt and approved reference files for one area of work. Stable, non-confidential context goes in the Project, the case goes in the chat. What is stored and for how long depends on plan and setting; check it first.

sections.title: Set up a Project brief
sections.content:
The system prompt has three parts: role and organization, communication rules, data and decision boundaries. For a sales Project:

```
I work in sales at an 80-person mechanical-engineering company
in Bavaria with customers in Germany and Austria.
Tone: pragmatic, plain and direct.
Use informal address for established customers and formal address for new customers.
Do not use promotional claims or superlatives.
Do not include real customer names or active negotiation margins.
Do not invent prices, dates or commitments.
```

An approved, sanitized 2024 quotation template can go in as a format example. Before every upload, check the rules on storage, access and retention.

sections.title: Artifacts as editable outputs
sections.content:
An Artifact shows the output in its own editable panel instead of the chat, depending on the product as a document, code, HTML, React component, SVG or Markdown. It saves copying between model and editor.

Factual, legal, technical and accessibility checks remain. Whether effort really drops, you measure on the actual task.

sections.title: Memory: what Claude keeps
sections.content:
What Claude keeps depends on product, plan and setting. Clarify first what is stored where, for how long, and how you delete it. Exercises use only fictional data such as "Customer Alpha (fictional), 80 employees, sample payment term."

**Not in Memory:** real customer or contact data without an approved basis and policy, confidential financial or contract data, passwords, tokens or API keys.

**Possible after policy review:** a non-confidential role description, general language and format preferences, approved standard tasks.

Curate the entries and review access and deletion regularly.

quiz.questionText: Which two persistent-context mechanisms does this lesson cover?
quiz.explanation: Project context applies within one Project; cross-chat Memory across conversations where product and settings support it.

quiz.questionText: What should never be stored in Claude Memory?

answerOptions.text: Passwords, access tokens and unapproved confidential data

quiz.explanation: No secrets. For customer, financial or contract data, your organization's data classification and tool policy come first.

lessons.subtitle: How system access works without connecting real accounts here

sections.title: A question that needs three sources
sections.content:
Monday, 7:00. Last week's commitments are scattered across emails, meeting notes and documents. Search one source and you miss the follow-up in another.

This lesson connects no real accounts. Gmail, Calendar and Drive supply sample data for the connector workflow: pick the source, minimize permissions, document the data flow, review the result.

sections.title: What connectors are
sections.content:
A connector is a managed integration between an AI interface and an external source, usually via OAuth: pick the account, inspect the scopes, approve access, revoke it on a schedule. Common sources are Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Notion, GitHub, Slack, Airtable, Salesforce, HubSpot, Stripe, Jira and Linear.

**Distinction from MCP:** product connectors are managed within a product interface. MCP is a protocol through which a compatible client uses tools and resources; deployment and control depend on server and client.

**GDPR:** settle purpose, legal basis, scopes, logging, deletion, DPA terms and a permission review before production use.

sections.title: The commitment-audit query
sections.content:
The exercise question:
> "From the sample emails of the last seven days, extract statements such as 'I will do X', 'we will deliver Y' or 'Z by Friday'. Check the sample calendar and Drive for documented follow-up. Return open commitments with sender, due date, status and source reference."

The pattern: constrain source and date range, extract commitments into a fixed schema, cross-check a second source, cite sources in the table, and a person reviews before any action.

A typical exercise result: 14 commitments, 9 completed and documented, 3 overdue, 2 unclear. The three overdue ones reach you as a review list; nothing goes out automatically.

sections.title: Access changes the risk boundary
sections.content:
Every connector trades copying for access, and access brings risk. Permissions, approved sources, logging and revocation are fixed before the first retrieval.

**Exercise prompts with sample data:**
- "Which fictional meetings are scheduled tomorrow? Give three preparation questions for each."
- "Draft a letter to Customer Alpha from the fictional meeting record."
- "List only the titles of attachments from Customer Alpha in the sample emails."

In production only with approved data, minimum scopes and human review.

quiz.questionText: What is the relevant distinction between a product connector and MCP?

answerOptions.text: A product manages the connector; MCP is a protocol interface for tools
Connectors always cost money; MCP is always free
Connectors can write; MCP can only read

quiz.explanation: A connector is configured within a product. MCP defines how a compatible client talks to tools and resources; either can run locally or remotely.

quiz.questionText: What can a connector improve compared with repeated manual uploads?

answerOptions.text: Retrieve authorized data without repeated copies; provider terms and privacy rules still apply

quiz.explanation: A connector saves copying and makes access scopes visible, but it is no GDPR exemption. You still check provider documentation, contract and data flow.

lessons.title: Skills: reusable commands for recurring work
lessons.subtitle: Turn repeated tasks into slash commands

props.title: Write the PROMPT.md for your Skill
props.scenario: You are a sales manager building a `/kunden-antwort` Skill. Replace the placeholder with a reproducible brief with role, context, input placeholder, format and exclusions.

criteria.label: Gives company context: industry, size and tone
Defines format: word limit or structure
Explicit exclusion: no prices or promotional language

sections.title: The SOP nobody reads
sections.content:
A standard operating procedure (SOP) helps only if someone finds and applies it, and under time pressure almost everyone skips the long document.

A Skill brings the instruction to where the work happens: you type `/angebot-draft` and the maintained procedure for an internal quotation draft runs the same way every time. The SOP owner, approvals and review evidence are still needed.

sections.title: What a Skill is
sections.content:
A Skill is a **named, reusable instruction package with optional tool access and hooks** for a defined task. In the course example it lives in `.claude/skills/skill-name/`, includes `SKILL.md`, `PROMPT.md` and `EXAMPLES.md`, and is invoked as `/skill-name` in the supported client. Directory and file layout depend on the client; check the current documentation.

**Three categories:**
1. **Output Skills** produce a draft (`/angebot-draft`, `/wochenbericht-auto`)
2. **Analysis Skills** structure input (`/meeting-summary-de`, `/invoice-parse`)
3. **Check Skills** compare against a rule (`/gdpr-audit`, `/eu-ai-act-classify`)

The course materials include examples of all three.

sections.title: Three files, one command
sections.content:
`/angebot-draft` in three files:

**SKILL.md**
```markdown
# /angebot-draft
Description: Creates an internal quotation draft.
Input: approved or fictional brief
Output: draft with marked price, date and approval fields
```

**PROMPT.md**
```
Create a quotation draft from a fictional or approved brief.
Do not invent prices, delivery commitments or contract terms.
Mark every open field for human review.
```

**EXAMPLES.md:** two or three clearly fictional examples, such as `Customer Alpha (fictional), 2 sample machines`.

Measure setup time, consistency and correction effort. Approval and sending stay manual.

sections.title: The three-times rule
sections.content:
If you do a task three times a month, check whether a Skill makes it more consistent. Add up setup, maintenance, execution and review; the Skill stays only if the test shows a benefit.

**Exercise:** Pick a task you completed at least three times this month and draft `SKILL.md`, `PROMPT.md` and `EXAMPLES.md`. Run the Skill with two different inputs, compare the results and refine.

quiz.questionText: When should you evaluate a recurring task for a Skill?

answerOptions.text: After one use in every case
After it recurs at least three times in a month
Only after ten uses per day

quiz.explanation: Three monthly occurrences are this course's trigger to evaluate. Whether the Skill pays off depends on setup, maintenance and review.

quiz.questionText: Which three files form the course's example Skill package?
quiz.explanation: SKILL.md holds the metadata, PROMPT.md the instructions and EXAMPLES.md the test cases.

lessons.title: Plugins and MCP: connecting Claude to systems
lessons.subtitle: Install plugins and configure MCP servers

sections.title: Installing is not approval
sections.content:
A plugin bundles Skills, MCP servers, hooks and sub-agents. A GitHub integration, for example, delivers repository search, pull-request review and issue actions through authenticated APIs. The output needs review, and every API action stops at your account's permissions.

**Vendor-maintained packages** have documented provenance and release ownership. For **community packages** you review code, permissions and updates yourself. Install only what the organization has approved, and only after checking source, version and requested permissions.

sections.title: Install a plugin
sections.content:
The setup as an exercise:

```bash
/plugin install github@claude-plugins-official
```

A supported client asks for user or Project scope, authentication, permissions and a restart. Check the command and package source before pressing Enter. Secrets do not belong in scripts or command arguments: use an approved secret store or interactive authentication, protect the configuration files and document revocation.

After an authorized connection:
> "Search the approved sample customer database for fictional companies in Bavaria with no activity for six months. Draft reactivation emails for five records and do not send them."

Retrieval, text generation and approval stay separate steps.

sections.title: MCP as a tool interface
sections.content:
**MCP means Model Context Protocol.** It defines how a compatible AI client calls external **tools**, such as `read_file`, `update_record` or `send_message`, and reads exposed **resources** such as files or data. Where no plugin exists, an MCP server can deliver the integration. Learning examples are `filesystem` (local files), `postgresql` (database) and `playwright` (browser automation).

In production every server needs its own security review: permissions, secret handling, logging, least privilege, revocation and human approval for consequential writes.

sections.title: Dry-run an MCP setup
sections.content:
The installation source has to be attributable and reviewed: no unknown script, no `curl | bash`. A clean test records configuration path, permissions, secret source, backup and startup check.

In the dry run you search only for a fictional term such as `Fiktivwerk Alpha` and expect no real registry result. Researching a real company needs an approved source, legal basis, search scope and purpose; you check every result against the legally authoritative primary source.

quiz.questionText: What is the relevant difference between a plugin and MCP?

answerOptions.text: A plugin bundles capabilities; MCP is a protocol for tools and resources
Plugins always cost money; MCP is always free

quiz.explanation: A plugin is a distribution package. MCP is a protocol that a plugin or standalone integration may use.

quiz.questionText: Why restrict installation to reviewed vendor packages or approved organization bundles?

answerOptions.text: Unknown scripts can compromise systems or expose secrets
Every community package is technically inferior

quiz.explanation: Unreviewed scripts can overwrite settings, exfiltrate secrets or give themselves persistent access.

lessons.title: Design Skill and Artifacts
lessons.subtitle: Outputs with a deliberate visual system

sections.title: Why AI output looks generic
sections.content:
Type "Build a landing page for my product" and typography, color, layout, hierarchy and motion stay open. The model fills the gaps with patterns found in generated interfaces and component defaults since 2023: Inter, an indigo gradient, a hero with three cards, one call to action for everything.

Each choice is defensible on its own. Together they show that nobody made a design decision, because the design brief was incomplete.

sections.title: Install the Design Skill and read its first output
sections.content:
Installation and invocation, as an example:

```
/plugin install frontend-design@claude-plugins-official

/frontend-design "Landing page for a mechanical-engineering company,
80 employees, audience: craft businesses with 10 to 30 employees,
35 years in operation, quality is prioritized over lowest price."
```

First comes a design direction, no code yet:

> - Direction: established industrial company with a current digital interface
> - Type: serif display face with a restrained sans-serif text face
> - Color: warm gray with a copper accent
> - Structure: image-led introduction, documented company story, evidence block
> - Motion: limited to purposeful state changes; no decorative parallax

The React and Tailwind draft comes only after your approval. Before integrating it, you check accessibility, responsiveness, content, dependencies and production fit.

sections.title: Two decisions instead of one
sections.content:
The Design Skill separates design direction from implementation. You can inspect the written direction and remove generic choices before any code exists; only what you approve gets built. The same brief carries other formats:

- **Presentation:** `/frontend-design "Ten-slide presentation on Q1 results. Audience: management. Focus: three Q2 decisions."`
- **Customer dashboard:** `/frontend-design "Dashboard for the status of a construction project. Show progress, next milestones and current blockers."`
- **Quotation as a web document:** `/frontend-design "One-page quotation with scope, reviewed price fields, references and an approval action."`

Every output needs its own accessibility, data and export checks.

sections.title: Design for non-designers
sections.content:
You set audience, hierarchy, tone, visual references and limits without React or CSS. You still check responsive behavior, semantic structure, keyboard access, contrast, loading, privacy and maintainability.

**Exercise:** Build a landing-page variant with fictional or approved content. Ask for three materially different design directions before you pick one, and export the Artifact only after testing at mobile and desktop widths.

quiz.questionText: What does the Design Skill separate?

answerOptions.text: All CSS frameworks from the project
SVG output from every other format

quiz.explanation: The design direction is reviewed first; code is generated only after it is accepted.

quiz.questionText: Why do generated landing pages often converge on the same patterns?

answerOptions.text: The prompt leaves typography, color and structure open, so defaults are reused
Every web designer uses the same template
CSS supports only three visual styles

quiz.explanation: Without project-specific limits the model uses the most common fonts, gradients and card layouts.

lessons.title: Claude Code for non-developers
lessons.subtitle: File and document workflows from the terminal

props.title: Which Claude Code instruction is adequately specified?
props.scenario: You have 120 PDFs in `~/rechnungen/2025/` and need a CSV with date, supplier, amount and line items. Which prompt defines a reviewable first attempt?

candidates.label: Option A: vague request
candidates.prompt: Can you read the invoices in this folder?
candidates.critique: Folder, fields, output format and error behavior are missing. The system must ask or guess.

candidates.label: Option B: partly specified
candidates.prompt: Read all PDFs in `~/rechnungen/2025/`, extract date, supplier and amount, and write the results to a CSV.
candidates.critique: Path, input type and three fields are set. Line items, parse errors, column names and validation are missing.

candidates.label: Option C: testable brief
candidates.prompt: Task: Read all PDFs in `~/rechnungen/2025/` without modifying them. Extract `datum` (ISO 8601), `lieferant` (string), `brutto` (EUR decimal), `netto` (EUR decimal) and `positionen` (JSON array with `beschreibung`, `menge`, `einzelpreis`). Write `~/rechnungen/2025_summary.csv` as UTF-8 comma-separated data. For parse failures, log the file name and error to stderr and continue. Final report: successful and failed counts plus the three largest supplier totals. Do not overwrite an existing output file.
candidates.critique: Source, schema, output, encoding, failure handling, overwrite protection and a reconciliation report are defined.

sections.title: What Claude Code actually is
sections.content:
Claude Code is an agent in the terminal that reads and edits files and calls configured tools. Beyond software it carries approved file and document workflows: renaming, sorting, merging and extracting files, reading PDFs, cleaning spreadsheets, OCR, batch processing with a fixed schema and error log, note and SOP workflows, reports from local sources.

What works depends on version, permissions and tools. Start in a copied test directory, limit access, keep backups and read every proposed action before approving it.

sections.title: First run: 80 invoices to CSV
sections.content:
Before setup, read the current installation, plan and authentication requirements at `code.claude.com` and use an approved Claude.ai account. Practice with fictional or redacted invoices in a copied directory:
> "In `~/Desktop/Rechnungen-2025/` there are 80 fictional PDF invoices. Read without modifying them. Extract date, amount, supplier and purpose. Write `Rechnungen-2025-export.csv` in the same directory, log parse failures and produce a count reconciliation."

Check plan and permissions first. Afterwards validate every failed record and a risk-based sample of the successful ones before moving to real data. Record execution time, review time and extraction errors on your hardware.

sections.title: Finished running does not mean correct
sections.content:
Extraction fails on bad scans, layout variation, OCR errors or corrupted files, and a run without a crash proves no value correct. Fix the checks first:
- reconcile input and output counts
- inspect every parse warning and missing required field
- validate totals against the source documents
- sample across suppliers, formats and confidence levels
- review consequential legal or financial fields completely

Automate more only when repeated runs hold a documented error threshold. Source files stay unchanged, outputs reversible.

sections.title: Three workflows from mid-sized companies
sections.content:
**Weekly report from notes:** Read approved notes from the last seven days in `50 Daily/` and summarize decisions, action items and lessons in a one-page draft with links to the source notes.

**Apprenticeship logs:** Run OCR on fictional photos in `~/Berichtshefte/`. Extract date, hours and work description into CSV, flag unreadable fields and leave signatures for manual handling.

**Letter drafts:** Prepare individualized draft letters from a fictional `Kunden.csv` in a new output directory. Send nothing, overwrite nothing.

Judge each workflow by runtime, error rate and review effort, including setup and approval.

quiz.questionText: Which Claude Code capabilities are relevant outside software development?

answerOptions.text: Only around ten percent of features
File operations, document analysis and controlled batch processing
None; Claude Code is only for developers

quiz.explanation: File operations, document extraction and batch processing work without a software project. There is no reliable percentage.

quiz.questionText: What is the appropriate validation strategy for a first batch-processing run?

answerOptions.text: Reconcile counts, review errors, sample by risk, fully review consequential fields
Never automate any check and repeat all work manually
Review only high-risk files and ignore parse warnings

quiz.explanation: Validate counts and errors, sample by risk and inspect every consequential field. Automate more only with documented evidence.

lessons.title: Memory and CLAUDE.md
lessons.subtitle: Maintain context without storing the wrong data

props.title: Build your CLAUDE.md: what belongs there?
props.scenario: Your budget: 2,500 tokens. Decide what persists in CLAUDE.md, what belongs in a chat or Skill, and what Claude must not get at all. More content can dilute important instructions.

blocks.label: Role, organization, industry and communication rules
blocks.description: Only stable, approved context relevant to the Project.

blocks.label: Active projects and goals, three to five lines each
blocks.description: Only current, non-confidential summaries, kept up to date.

blocks.label: Working rules: never X, always Y, no unapproved prices
blocks.description: Stable boundaries the workflow must always apply.

blocks.label: Team names, roles and responsibilities
blocks.description: Optional, subject to data policy; roles instead of names where names are unnecessary.

blocks.label: Summaries of the last ten chats
blocks.description: Do not copy automatically. Case-specific context stays in the chat or maintained record.

blocks.label: All customers with revenue and contact details
blocks.description: Leave it out: persistent instructions are not an approved customer database.

blocks.label: Skill index with short names and one-sentence descriptions
blocks.description: A short index helps route work to maintained Skills.

blocks.label: Five favorite prompt templates
blocks.description: Recurring instructions belong in tested Skills instead of CLAUDE.md.

sections.title: Storing everything is not a solution
sections.content:
Without persistent instructions you retype organization and style rules in every conversation. Store everything and you get privacy, accuracy and maintenance problems. Two mechanisms sit in between:

**CLAUDE.md** is a reviewable, versionable Markdown instruction file that Claude Code loads according to the client's current file-discovery and precedence rules.

**Cross-chat Memory** is a product feature that, when enabled, keeps selected information across conversations. Availability, behavior and controls change with product, plan and date.

Neither is a security boundary. You verify loading, access, retention and deletion in the current product.

sections.title: Build a CLAUDE.md
sections.content:
A CLAUDE.md with clearly fictional data:

```markdown
# CLAUDE.md: Fictional sales role

## Context
- Fictional User Alpha, sales for fictional sample products
- Organization: Fiktivwerk Beispiel GmbH (fictional)

## Language and format
- English, plain, concise and pragmatic

## Data boundaries
- No real customer, financial or access data
- Prices, dates and commitments remain placeholders until approval

## Tools
- Use only explicitly approved, least-privileged tools
- No external messages or write actions without approval
```

Check when and from which path your client loads Project instructions. The file does not enforce permissions.

sections.title: Curate cross-chat Memory
sections.content:
Open your product's Memory settings and read what is in there:
- `Fictional User Alpha prefers English`: verify, correct if needed
- `Fictional User works on Fiktivwerk Alpha`: too specific, delete it

Store only what is necessary and non-confidential, delete anything without a current purpose, and check accuracy, access and deletion regularly. Menus and features change.

sections.title: What never ends up in Memory
sections.content:
Third-party data, credentials and confidential business information go into persistent Memory only if an approved purpose, legal basis, product configuration and retention policy explicitly allow it.

**Normally stays out:** customer names and contact details, account numbers, third-party email addresses, margins and negotiation strategies, HR records.

**Possible after policy review:** your public role and organization, general style preferences, approved tools, typical non-confidential task categories.

Every entry brings obligations on accuracy, access and deletion.

quiz.questionText: Which two persistent-context mechanisms are covered here?
quiz.explanation: CLAUDE.md provides Project instructions under the client's loading rules. Cross-chat Memory is controlled through product settings.

quiz.questionText: What does not belong in persistent Memory without explicit approval and controls?

answerOptions.text: A public description of your role
Third-party personal data, customer records, confidential financial data

quiz.explanation: Persistent Memory is no customer database and no HR system. Purpose, legal basis, access and retention come before any personal data.
